items.title: Filmmaker Sraiyanti on Auto Queens and the ‘amount of power women feel when together’
items.summary: Propped up on a boat resting on the shore, looking out at the evening sea, Leela and Mohana eat their meals and joke about fish. “I have older fish because I am older and you have young fish because you are younger,” Leela, adorable and funny as she is with Mohana, says, laughing. Two auto-rickshaw drivers relaxing at the end of a working day is how Auto Queens , a documentary on the camaraderie and struggles of a group of women workers in Chennai, begins. The film, made by cinematographer-director Sraiyanti, was screened at the International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Kerala on September 26. “The idea came to me from a friend, Mathivannan, who is one of the producers. Their company was doing some work with Veera Pengal Munnetra Sangam (VPMS), the women-led auto rickshaw and transport workers union in Chennai,” Sraiyanti says. The VPMS began as a Whatsapp group in 2018 to address the many issues faced by women rickshaw drivers, including a lack of parking space. It was later registered in 2024.
